scope: All twenty-five development source migrations: four Python final/restart sources, nine read-only MJS sources, two SDK Session replay sources, one recovery source, three ordinary lifecycle sources, one Runtime-loss source, one metadata-browser source, one Runtime deployment source, two Controller deployment sources and one Temporal deployment source. All originals individually verified, archived and removed; no retained deployment or restart. Final Runtime recovery and overall storage/regression audit are complete, with scope and evidence in the cache exit report.
intentional_changes: Configuration/mode/storage checks before external commands
Exactly five lifecycle, three publication and one replay Trace; unique files/IDs and report correlation
Publication cutoff applies to its group regardless of filenames
Fixed process selectors including normalized and bare entry filenames, excluding checker and real ancestors
Private final output files are not overwritten

Controller saved reports bind Agent/Session/Runtime/Trace identities before external reads; live SQL binds Session ownership, and Runtime labels plus a complete RW workspace volume and resolved marker path are checked

Read-only MJS drivers validate full configuration and fixed output leaves before HTTP, reject non-regular inputs and existing/symlink reports, and recheck before exclusive private writes. reportBasename preserves custom Agent snapshot names.

Parameterized HTTP reports bind Agent and rejected Session identities; chat Trace IDs are valid and unique. Count expectations remain within the original Jaeger limit. Historical strict failures remain unchanged.

Replay validates full configuration and all output leaves before Docker; Session database ownership/cwd and exactly one actual load request are bound to configuration. Encoded history is decoded before login/load.

Raw replay Trace snapshots may update only the current writer's own regular file, verified by inode/device and O_NOFOLLOW; existing reports remain protected. Historical replay restores original PGDMP rows and retains strict results.

Recovery validates configuration, SHA-256 manifest and all four output leaves before external calls. Its only executed operation remains one rebuild; unused publications/other lifecycle helpers were removed without inventing new scenarios.

Recovery binds Runtime name/full Docker ID/managed label/Agent/scope and expected complete RW workspace volume; nested mounts and HostConfig.Tmpfs cannot shadow it. Runtime execution IDs are not Docker IDs. Whole-workspace find/hash failures propagate before sorting; historical warnings remain strict failures.

Ordinary lifecycle validates all configuration/output leaves before HTTP; binds created/returned Agent and full Runtime identity/scope/RW workspace volume before marker writes; resolves marker paths inside workspace and outside cache. Trace and request IDs are unique, and lifecycle polling updates only writer-owned files.

Ordinary lifecycle uses the corrected publication root selector for all three originals. It preserves raw publication evidence after structural checks but before unexpected-warning failure. Three historical reports match with all fifteen lifecycle strict failures preserved.

Runtime-loss reads both snapshots before effects; Compose project/service/scope binds the restarted Controller identity and environment, and scope is derived rather than a new caller field. The validated start cutoff filters search and is rechecked in collected publication details.

Runtime-loss preserves normal stop -t 10, exit-zero/no-OOM evidence before removal, exited/absent/offline observation, source generation and five absence probes. Agent/App state, full Runtime/RW workspace identity and distinct lifecycle/publication IDs are validated; historical report and five strict failures remain unchanged.

Metadata browser validates complete configuration, three credentials, same-origin workspace URL and unique matching Agent/Session parameters before browser or HTTP effects. Browser report fallback does not require a passing earlier Trace check. Three output leaves are exclusive/private; screenshot buffers support directories with spaces.

Metadata keeps all two-page/list/reload/history/rejection assertions. SIGINT/SIGTERM stops in-memory polling and saves Interrupted; close failures still save a failed report. Nine real UI/Chromium/local-ACP cases preserve historical report fields without claiming original browser-frame or deployed Provider replay. The fixture requires a fresh durable output root before building.

Runtime deployment preserves before/deploy/restart/after, whole-daemon assertions, four complete ACP row maps, three verified database archives and whole-workspace hashing. Fresh mode outputs and a private hashed context bind configuration/baseline; effective Compose and full container IDs are rechecked before mutations. Dumps are exclusive/private and validated through the same descriptor; find/hash failures propagate with unchanged empty-manifest bytes. Stop/backup/promotion/start/report/interruption failures recover known containers while preserving the original error, including Compose observation failures. Actual report counts are computed. All 95 Python support tests and 18 stateful entry tests pass; five actual Docker cases pass on owned shell services/PostgreSQL. The shared daemon global after correctly rejects stopped retained containers; its positive path is proven by the whole-daemon component model. No retained service is deployed or restarted.

Controller 20260921 retains whole-daemon running-container scope, original five mount fields, networks, candidate deployment with 120-second Compose wait, three archives and original four-table rows while allowing additions. Explicit workspace/recovery paths, private baseline context, effective Compose and full IDs bind all stages. The five-field recovery record must authorize exactly the configured Runtime replacement and RW volume; no invented generation or strict-Trace requirement. Computed report counts replace copied constants. Failed deployment, normal interruption and missing-container creation failures recover only bound or confirmed-absent targets and retain original failure. 95 support plus 30 integration tests pass, followed by 12 focused tests after snapshot-oracle extraction; six actual Docker cases and exact legacy snapshot/report-field compatibility pass. Historical after remains a pre-recovery expected failure, and stopped historical full inspect is not promoted to a healthy baseline.

Controller 20260917 retains both service modes in either order, whole-daemon running snapshots, three online archives, original-row preservation with additions, unchanged Runtime/non-target IDs and all original final business assertions. Shared context/output/identity/rollback mechanics are used with per-service completed records; a failed target never rolls back its already deployed sibling. Explicit report paths bind before capture, while final validates Agent/Session/Runtime/workspace ownership, exactly two schema rejections, complete marker bytes, temporary resources and process absence. Resolved marker paths cannot enter cache. Success files follow all final checks. 96 support and 38 integration tests, nine actual Docker cases, six rerun single-service Docker cases and both legacy snapshot/report comparisons pass. The one earlier observer process-group PermissionError remains recorded; no descendants remained, all 16 targeted observer tests and the full gate passed afterward. Historical browser failure and five lifecycle strict failures remain unchanged; no retained deployment or live historical business replay is claimed.

Temporal retains before/deploy/restart/resume/after, whole-daemon snapshots, exact four-table maps and complete workspace hashing. Temporal local already points to candidate at baseline; Agent Controller image stays old. Stop Controller then Temporal, verify four archives while both stopped, start Temporal healthy before Controller. Context/full IDs and fresh private outputs bind stages; same-ID restart and readiness-only resume retain their distinct contracts. A validated resume record completes partial deployment. Candidate mounts/networks and readiness are checked immediately. Failed deployment restores old services in dependency order and retains failure; missing old containers use a private override with pinned old image IDs and saved old healthchecks because the old Temporal image lacks readiness.sh. 96 support and 50 integration tests pass; eight actual Docker cases validate four archives, whole-workspace bytes, stop/restart/resume, backup/candidate/missing-container recovery and find/hash errors. Global after correctly rejects retained stopped containers; its positive is proven by the complete daemon component model. Legacy baseline/deployment records and four PGDMP hashes match, while the earlier Compose-start failure and saved resume/restart outcomes remain unchanged. No missing latest after/restart inspection or fresh historical business replay is invented.

Runtime missing-target follow-up: old-image recreation requires successful exact-name absence checks before and immediately before Compose, unchanged effective Compose and all other baseline full IDs/names. Unknown replacements, late arrivals and failed daemon queries reject. Recovery success retains original failure; recovery failure chains it. 22 flow tests, 96 support/54 integration tests and six actual Docker cases pass. The real case removes only the bound fixture container after normal exit, recovers a healthy new container on the old image, preserves other resources and leaves no successful deployment report.
